symptoms: Customer experience raised a request for an explanatory chatbot about late parcels (CL-01).
300 of 1000 tracked orders (30%) are recorded as late at the handover stage in order-db (E-02).
290 orders were released from the warehouse only after their scheduled carrier pickup had already occurred (E-04).
21 of 30 RELEASE-BATCH job runs failed in the warehouse job log (E-04).
Carrier pickup log independently shows a median pickup delay of 2.0 hours across 60 pickups (E-01).
causal_chain: Warehouse RELEASE-BATCH job runs fail frequently: 21 of 30 runs failed (E-04).
As a result, 290 orders are released from the warehouse only after their scheduled carrier pickup window has already passed (E-04).
This produces handover-stage lateness recorded in order-db: 300 of 1000 orders (30%) late at handover (E-02), a count close to the 290 released-after-pickup orders.
The carrier's own pickup log separately shows a median 2.0h pickup delay (E-01), a co-occurring but non-causal symptom given the warehouse release already lagged the scheduled pickup.
Customers perceive their parcels as late and request an explanation, prompting the initial chatbot request (CL-01).

assumptions.statement: The near-equal counts of orders released after pickup (290, E-04) and late handover orders (300, E-02) refer to largely the same population of orders, implying a causal link rather than coincidental overlap.

DA-ORD, DA-PICK and DA-WMS, despite having UNKNOWN completeness, are sufficiently complete to ground accurate customer-facing lateness explanations.
